title: Boot write probe, typed storage refusals, api key redaction
kind: code slice, not an acceptance run — nothing here is lab-observed

closes.a24_finding_1: no write probe on the boot path: an instance boots green on a credential that cannot store a byte
closes.a24_finding_2: a write refusal and a bucket-full refusal are both a bare 500 internal_error
closes.a24_finding_3: the api's request logger writes the full storage key where the worker's redacts it (the api half of A35's open object_key/storage_key item)
closes.a24_finding_4: docs/evidence/*.sh is linted by nothing in meta CI

vidra-core.scope: the three code defects plus the OpenAPI prose

vidra-user.ordering: MERGE IMMEDIATELY AFTER core#196; the contract lane on main goes red the moment core merges

vidra.scope: .github/workflows/meta-ci.yml lint loop; AGENTS.md rule 7 invoked deliberately — the lint gap IS the task

sc1_boot_write_probe.seam: cmd/api boot, synchronous, immediately before resolveBucketOwnership; then storage.WriteHealth.Run on its own ticker
sc1_boot_write_probe.cadence: storage.WriteProbeInterval = 5 minutes, its OWN ticker, started in EVERY role
sc1_boot_write_probe.why_not_the_settings_poller: the poller is role-gated and is never constructed in worker-role processes, and the worker is the process whose ability to write must not go unwatched (a transcode can run for minutes before its first PUT)
sc1_boot_write_probe.cost_per_probe: one PUT and one DELETE of a 60-byte object under .vidra/write-probe/<rand>, outside every swept prefix, removed immediately
sc1_boot_write_probe.boot_behaviour: a failed probe does NOT abort boot — an instance that cannot store bytes still serves every video it has and the admin console needed to fix the credential

component.name: storage
component.distinct_from: the existing s3 component, which is BucketExists (a HeadBucket) — s3 asks whether the bucket is there, storage asks whether this instance can write to it

states.not_configured: no monitor wired, or wired and not yet probed (never a fault)
states.ok: the last probe stored and removed an object
states.degraded: the store took the write and refused the DELETE — writable, but a half-granted key (B2 grants deleteFiles separately from writeFiles)
states.down: the last probe was refused; Error carries the class sentence and never the provider's text

readiness_semantics.convention_followed: handleReady takes an instance out of rotation for PostgreSQL and NOTHING else; Redis down is degraded-with-200 because every limiter fails open and 503ing on a shared Redis would empty every replica out of rotation at once
readiness_semantics.storage_decision: the same argument applies to a SHARED bucket, so storage down reports the instance `degraded` with HTTP 200, not 503
readiness_semantics.component_severity: down rather than degraded, because a store that will not accept a write is not impaired, it is unable

worker_behaviour.gate: transcode.WithStorageWriteGate, checked BEFORE the claim, beside the scratch floor
worker_behaviour.log: transcode: deferring all jobs, the object store is not accepting writes  class=<class>
worker_behaviour.why: a claim against an unwritable store spends a full encode and one of five attempts on a condition the video did not cause; five ticks dead-letter it permanently. Deferring leaves jobs 'pending' so restoring the credential drains them with no operator action
worker_behaviour.unprobed_is_writable: an unprobed or unwired monitor answers writable — no evidence is not evidence of a refusal, and this gate must never be the reason work stops on an instance nobody has asked yet

never_logged: the object key of any media
the access key id or secret
sc1_boot_write_probe.log_discipline: a line is emitted only on a CHANGE of verdict — a store refusing for a week does not repeat every five minutes, and a recovery is never silent

sc2_typed_refusals.classification_site: internal/storage, at the backend boundary (S3.PutSized/Open/Delete/Exists/ListKeys/DeletePrefix/EnsureBucket, Local.Put/Open/Delete/DeletePrefix)
sc2_typed_refusals.http_mapping: 503 storage_unavailable, from the CENTRAL error handler, so every media-writing path answers it — direct upload, resumable finalize, replace, thumbnails, captions, avatars, playlist covers

write_denied.body: this instance's media store refused to accept the file: the configured credential can read the store but not write to it, so nothing can be uploaded, generated or transcoded until that is fixed. Grant the storage key permission to put and delete objects (on Backblaze B2, writeFiles and deleteFiles are granted separately), or check that the configured bucket is the one the key is scoped to, then retry — nothing was stored and nothing was lost

s3: any answer whose text contains 'quota exceeded'
quota_exceeded.body: this instance's media store has no room left — its bucket quota or its disk is full — so the file could not be stored. Free space or raise the quota, then retry: nothing was stored and nothing was lost

unreachable.body: this instance cannot reach its media store right now, so the file could not be stored. This is usually a network path or an endpoint setting rather than anything about the file; retry shortly — nothing was stored and nothing was lost

implementation_notes: the classifier reaches the SDK's answer with errors.As, NOT minio.ToErrorResponse — that helper is a bare type switch with no unwrapping, so it answers an empty ErrorResponse for every error already wrapped with op/key context, which is every error a caller sees

the quota pass runs BEFORE the status-code pass: a bucket quota is the least standardised answer in the S3 API and MinIO's arrives as a 4xx that a forbidden-means-denied rule would otherwise swallow, sending an operator to fix permissions on a full bucket

classification WRAPS rather than replaces: Error() renders the provider's sentence with the class appended, so the operator log keeps everything it had and the worker's bounded-retry line names the class for free
ErrNotFound and ErrInvalidKey are never classified — a classified ErrNotFound would turn every missing thumbnail into a 503
an unrecognised provider answer is left UNCLASSIFIED and stays a 500: a class nobody can act on sends an operator to the wrong place
sc2_typed_refusals.no_half_write_invariant: pinned by TestAttachOriginalOnARefusedWriteLeavesNoHalfWrittenRow for BOTH causes: video stays state=draft, 0 video_files rows, 0 daily-quota ledger appends

sc3_key_redaction.seam_reused: internal/jobstatus.RedactDetail — the same function the worker's job logger and internal/jobtrace already use; not forked, not reimplemented
sc3_key_redaction.result: storage: s3: put "[redacted-key]": Access Denied. — the cause survives, the key does not; URLs, credential-shaped pairs and email addresses in a driver's error are stripped too

guard.name: TestObjectKeyLogValuesAreRedacted
guard.mechanism: AST walk over every non-test file in the module; an object-key-shaped log field whose value is not a Redact* call (or a string literal) fails the build
guard.exempt: marker_key — its value is the constant .vidra/owner, and redacting a constant only makes the boot line harder to read
guard.proved_red: unwrapping internal/mediahash/service.go:115 made it fail with the file:line; restoring the wrap made it pass
